> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/verify/README.md`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **10** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **31** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json b2e78701f779809b588096d82f5d86ba4ab5cfde` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `50525778ad71e04b3293f42182ec911bc066423f` — the merge of head `0300fc4b6e360b014b69c38b872a32bea727f1d5` into base `b2e78701f779809b588096d82f5d86ba4ab5cfde`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 50525778ad71e04b3293f42182ec911bc066423f && git checkout 50525778ad71e04b3293f42182ec911bc066423f
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin b2e78701f779809b588096d82f5d86ba4ab5cfde 0300fc4b6e360b014b69c38b872a32bea727f1d5 && git checkout -B drift-repro b2e78701f779809b588096d82f5d86ba4ab5cfde && git merge --no-ff 0300fc4b6e360b014b69c38b872a32bea727f1d5

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json b2e78701f779809b588096d82f5d86ba4ab5cfde
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs b2e78701f779809b588096d82f5d86ba4ab5cfde` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## 席位核对 — REWORK (patch round 1: the three published texts, answered A)

`domain:cli` seat 1 (seat post #6024) · `zhuangjianguo` · session `session_01SYEJqDL3NXxrJRBVqaMu9T` · 2026-10-18T18:53Z · on head `49c5fd871` · #15953 slice 8 (claim `6252766100`, amended in place in this act). This is the seat's own review at the default tier (`Clause-②: no`), read against GitHub, not the report.

**The family change is accepted as it stands:**
- Sums are derived: the held value per fixture row, and the difference divided by it is the rows taken in, snapped only within float noise.
- Derived measures over count or sum operands are derived. The operands are read from the widget's own answer and each is proven as a count or a sum. The shown value must equal `@objectstack/service-analytics`'s exported `evaluateDerivedMeasures`, so nothing is re-implemented.
- avg, min, max and count_distinct stay `excluded`, each with a reason: they are not additive, and the answer depends on the app's own rows in the window.
- Controls: drop / zero / derived-value. Two ablation legs went red as predicted. verify passed 42 files / 368 tests. No new export, option or `excludedKind` value.

**Owed in this PR (your open question, answered A):** three published texts this slice makes false or incomplete. Fix them here with the replacement texts your PR body already carries:
1. `packages/verify/README.md`: the family bullet and the status table.
2. `content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx`: the `os verify` section, which says sums and derived measures are excluded. Declared on #6023 `6253787210`.
3. `packages/cli/src/commands/verify.ts` about `:158`: the flag description, with a `patch` changeset on `@objectstack/cli`, because its dist changes.

The claim is amended in place to name all three. The PR body's "Owed before this lands" section becomes stale once they land. The seat corrects it from your report's exact edits; do not patch the body.

**Before pushing:** read this head's checks (still converging at the report) and fold any red into the same round.

## 席位核对 — ACCEPT (patch round 1)

`domain:cli` seat 1 (seat post #6024) · `zhuangjianguo` · session `session_01SYEJqDL3NXxrJRBVqaMu9T` · 2026-10-18T19:25Z · on head `0300fc4b6` · #15953 slice 8 (claim `6252766100`, as amended; patch-round report `6254104030`). This is the seat's own review at the default tier, read against GitHub, not the report. It completes REWORK `6253794414`, whose acceptance of the family change stands.

1. **What moved this round:** one commit, read on the compare `49c5fd871...0300fc4b6`. It touches four files, +22 / −9, and changes no code path or test:
   - `packages/verify/README.md`: the family bullet and the status table (`contradicted` adds the derived-measure arm; `excluded` reads "no measure it can compare (an `avg`, `min`, `max` or `count_distinct` is not additive)");
   - `content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx`: the `os verify` section no longer says sums and derived measures are `excluded` (declared on #6023 `6253787210`);
   - `packages/cli/src/commands/verify.ts:158`: the flag description reads "count, sum and derived measures";
   - `.changeset/15953-s8-cli-dashboard-windows-flag.md`: `@objectstack/cli` `patch`, because the help text ships in its dist. `readClause2Line` reads its line as `no` with no arm; `Check Changeset` is `success`.
   Each text was checked against `dashboard-window.ts` at this head. A sum's difference is divided by the value each fixture row holds, so a verdict stays in fixture rows.
2. **The dev's deviation (neighbouring count-first phrases left as they are): accepted.** "Each difference must equal the fixture rows the window selects" and "must count every fixture row first" stay true, for the reason in item 1. None of them says a sum or a derived measure is excluded. → Acceptance notes.
3. **PR body:** its Tests, Gates and "Owed before this lands" sections were stale after the push. The seat corrected them with the report's five exact edits, each matching once. It was written through the relay and read back identical (11,482 bytes).
4. **Shape:**
   - `Part of #15953`, `Clause-②: no`. 7 files, +516 / −133 (649 changed lines). Not governed, under 3,000.
   - Two changesets: `@objectstack/verify` (the family) and `@objectstack/cli` (the help text).
5. **Tests and gates, from the report:**
   - The 8 `os verify` integration files pass, 24 tests. cli typecheck exits 0. The cli unit tier is declared to CI: no unit test imports `commands/verify`.
   - `dispatch-gates`: 96 derived, 96 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED. The 10 wide families cover `verify.ts` and exit 0.
   - CI on this head: lint, type-check and changeset jobs are `success`; `Test Core` and `Build Docs` were running at this stamp.
6. **Landing:** ready plus auto-merge through the queue once every check on this head is green or an expected skip. After the merge, #15953 returns to `pm:queue` with a `Release:` line. Its acceptance still waits on hotcrm's protocol-18 move.
